title: Coronary angiography
what: A thin tube is passed through an artery in your wrist or groin up to your heart. Contrast dye is injected, and the heart's blood vessels are seen on X-ray. You stay awake, with local anesthesia.
why: For chest pain, after a heart attack, if other tests showed problems with the heart's blood vessels, or before heart surgery.
duration: usually 30 to 60 minutes; in hospital from a few hours to 1 or 2 days
tell_doctor: Allergies to contrast dye, iodine, or medicines
Diabetes and which medicines you take for it. The doctor will tell you what to do
Blood thinners. Do not stop them on your own

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, including kidney function, and an ECG. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 4 to 6 hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact time.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Take your usual morning medicines only as your doctor says. Do not stop anything on your own.

prepare.title: Things to pack
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, slippers, your ID, and a list of your medicines.

bring: Your referral, test results, and ECG
Hospital discharge papers and your cardiologist's reports
steps: A thin tube called an IV is put into a vein. You may get a calming medicine
You lie on a table under the X-ray machine
The skin on your wrist or groin is numbed
Through a tiny puncture, a thin tube goes into the artery and up to your heart
Contrast dye is injected, and X-ray pictures are taken
Sometimes a stent is placed right away, if the doctor discussed this with you beforehand
The tube is removed, and a tight bandage is put on the puncture site
feel: The numbing shot lasts a few seconds
You do not feel the tube inside your blood vessels
With the contrast dye: a wave of warmth through your body. This is normal
If you get chest pain or trouble breathing, tell the doctor right away
after: A wrist bandage usually stays for a few hours. If the groin was used, you lie with your leg straight for a few hours
You are usually told to drink more water, so the dye leaves faster. The doctor will say how much
For a few days, do not lift heavy things with that arm or leg
Drive only when your doctor allows
The doctor usually explains the results right away
red_flags: The puncture site bleeds or swelling grows fast: press on it and call emergency services
Your arm or leg turns cold, pale, or numb
Chest pain or shortness of breath: call emergency services

faq.q: Is coronary angiography done under general anesthesia?
faq.a: Usually not. You stay awake, and only the puncture site is numbed. You may get a calming medicine.

faq.q: How is angiography different from a stent?
faq.a: Angiography is a look at the blood vessels. A stent is treatment: a small mesh tube is placed in the narrow spot. Sometimes both are done at once.

reminders.text: Coronary angiography tomorrow. Bring your test results, ECG, and medicine list. Eat only until the time your clinic gave you. Take medicines as your doctor said.
